title: Lesson 9: Tools and Skills: What Ships with Hermes, How to Extend It, and How to Know What's Real
description: Separating what an agent can do from how it does it well, treating the tool registry as a claim and the running agent as the evidence, and extending an agent by teaching it the client's rules.

questions.question: What is the difference between an agent's tools and its skills?
options: Tools are the actions an agent can take, and skills are the procedures it follows
Tools are the procedures an agent follows, and skills are the actions it can take
Tools are the credentials an agent stores, and skills are the toolsets it turns on
Tools are the on-demand documents an agent loads, and skills are the commands it may run
questions.explanation: Tools are the verbs an agent can execute, while skills carry the procedures that make it act the client's way, and the two fail differently when missing.

questions.question: An agent is said to ship with a broad set of tools. Why should that availability be treated as a claim rather than a guarantee?
options: Because every agent running on a given platform is guaranteed to receive the same complete set of tools
Because the registry lists tools that were quietly removed in the most recent software release
Because availability depends on the platform, the credentials present, and which toolsets are enabled
Because tools become unavailable whenever the agent is run without a person watching the session
questions.explanation: The platform, the credentials present, and a disabled toolset all stand between the registry and a live session, so the running agent is the real evidence.

questions.question: What makes a capability real, rather than merely claimed?
options: The agent giving a clear and confident description of the work it believes it performed
Evidence it actually fired, such as a tool call, an artifact, or output you can inspect
The capability appearing in the software's published list of features and supported tools
The agent confirming that it has completed the task and reporting the result as done
questions.explanation: A capability is real only when it leaves evidence of having fired; a confident summary is not proof that a tool ran.
